transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um, yeah—so the main thing is I get pulled off track really easily. Like I’ll be working on a dashboard I’m supposed to finish, and then one Slack ping comes in, or I hear a song lyric, or I suddenly think of a totally different project, and then I’ve completely lost what I was doing. It’s frustrating because I’ll be sitting there like, wait, what was I even in the middle of?

Do you often act on impulse without thinking things through, or find it really hard to stay focused on tasks that require sustained mental effort, like organizing your work or following detailed instructions?

Yeah, the staying focused part for sure. Like I’ll sit down to read a research article for class or watch a UX tutorial, and I think I’m paying attention, but then a few minutes later I realize my eyes have just been moving across the page or the video is still playing and I have no idea what I actually took in. It’s like when you walk into a room and forget why, except it’s with reading—which is annoying because some of the UX videos are actually interesting, like the ones about app layouts, but then I’ll notice the instructor has moved on to a whole different section and I’m just… lost.
Do you often feel restless, like you need to be moving or doing something, even in situations where it’s expected that you sit still?

Yeah, I do. Like if I’m in a long Zoom call or I’m supposed to just sit quietly and work in one spot, I get this kind of uncomfortable pressure in my body, like I need to stand up or pace around or at least do something with my hands.

It’s not always dramatic, but it’s hard to ignore. I’ll start thinking about how stiff the chair feels, or I’ll mess with a pen or my sleeves, and then I’m like—wait, I’m supposed to be paying attention, not reorganizing my desk or whatever.
Have you noticed yourself feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy, especially when you're struggling with staying on track or getting things done?

I don’t know if I’d say hopeless, exactly. I mean, I get frustrated with myself when I’m not getting stuff done, and then I’ll kind of spiral into being annoyed, like, “Why can’t I just finish this?” But I don’t think it’s the same as losing interest in everything.

Like, I’ll still want to do things I like… though sometimes I put them off too, which is weird because it’s stuff I actually enjoy. But then I’ll end up scrolling or reorganizing something random, like my desktop folders, and suddenly it’s an hour later. So… I guess more frustrated than down? I’m not totally sure what counts.
Do you often feel irritable or have strong emotional reactions, especially when things aren’t going the way you expect or you’re struggling to focus?

I’m not totally sure. I mean, I can get annoyed when something isn’t working, like if I’m trying to follow instructions and they’re written in this weird confusing way—actually, that happened with a design program tutorial once where the buttons didn’t match the video, and then I spent way too long clicking around.

But… strong emotional reactions? I don’t know. I wouldn’t say I’m exploding at people or anything. It’s more like I get irritated in the moment, then sometimes I’m distracted by something else and it kind of passes. I guess I haven’t really tracked it.
Do these difficulties with focus and restlessness happen mainly at work or in other settings too, like when you’re at home or trying to relax?

I’m not totally sure how to separate it, honestly. Like, I’m not working right now, so I don’t have a super clear “work versus home” comparison.

At home it can happen, I think… but then home is also where I’m doing school stuff or trying to relax, and those kind of blend together. Like I’ll sit down to watch something and then somehow I’m also checking my phone, getting up for water, remembering I should move laundry—actually I always forget laundry in the washer, which is so annoying—but yeah, I guess I don’t really have a clean answer.

So… not just one setting, probably? But I haven’t really paid attention to it that way.
When did you first start noticing these issues with focus and restlessness? Were they something you experienced as a child, or did they develop more recently as an adult?

I think it was pretty early, honestly. Like elementary school early. I don’t remember all of it super clearly, but my parents still have some of my old report cards somewhere—actually my mom keeps everything in this giant folder, it’s kind of intense—and teachers would write stuff like I rushed through worksheets or didn’t follow all the directions.

I also remember getting in trouble during group work because I’d talk over people, not like trying to be rude, I just kind of jumped in. And homework was a whole thing. My parents would sit next to me because if they didn’t, I’d wander off or start doing something else before finishing. So yeah, I don’t think it just started recently.
Can you describe any situations where your restlessness or impulsivity has led to problems in completing everyday tasks or interacting with others?

Yeah, I think in group projects especially. Like when people are brainstorming—this happens a lot with design stuff—I’ll get an idea and just kind of say it before they’re done explaining theirs. Or if we’re in Figma, I might start moving things around or adding to the board because I’m excited and I can already picture it.

And then afterward I’m like, oh… that probably looked really pushy. I don’t mean it that way, I’m not trying to take over, but I think it can come across like I’m not listening or like I’m rushing everyone. Figma is kind of dangerous for that because it’s so easy to just click and start changing things, and then suddenly I’ve interrupted the whole flow.
Do you often feel like your thoughts are racing or that you're constantly mentally 'revved up,' even when you're trying to relax or focus on something simple?

Yeah, sort of. It’s not always like dramatic racing thoughts, but I do feel kind of… mentally switched on a lot.

Like on days when I don’t have class or any real schedule, I’ll still end up bouncing from editing a prototype to cleaning my desk to opening some random dataset I meant to look at. And then I’m like, wait, wasn’t I supposed to be resting? But resting feels weird unless I’m actively doing something.

Even if I’m trying to relax, I’ll start thinking of things I could fix or start, and then I’m up doing them before I really decide to.

Can you tell me if these issues with getting distracted or feeling restless happen in different parts of your life, like when you're at school, at home, or working on personal projects, or if they mostly happen in one specific situation?

It’s definitely not just one setting. I mean, the main reason I came in is that I get pulled off track so easily pretty much anywhere.

Like, if I’m working on a dashboard, one Slack ping can completely derail me. Or even a song lyric will make me think of something else, and then suddenly I’m looking that up, or I’ll get a random idea for another project and it feels urgent for some reason. And then I come back and I’m like… wait, what was I even doing?

It happens with school stuff and personal projects too. Actually dashboards are a good example because there are so many little pieces, and I’ll start adjusting one chart and then remember some totally different thing I wanted to try, and then I’ve lost the thread of what I was supposed to be finishing.
Do you often fidget, tap your hands or feet, or squirm in your seat, especially when you’re trying to stay still or focus on something?

Yeah, definitely. I don’t always notice I’m doing it at first, but in meetings or portfolio reviews I’m usually bouncing my leg or clicking a pen, or twisting my rings around.

Sometimes I’ll realize because someone glances at my hands, and then I’m like, oh, sorry, I’m doing that again. Or I’ll be shifting around in the chair a lot. It’s kind of funny because portfolio reviews are already stressful, and then I’m trying to look composed, but my body is just… not cooperating.
Do you also have trouble staying focused or feel restless during social activities, like hanging out with friends or watching a movie together?

Yeah, I think so. Like if I’m supposed to be doing something quiet with other people, like watching a movie, I’ll kind of end up needing to do something else at the same time.

Even when I try to relax on my own, like reading or doing one of those calm sketching exercises, it doesn’t stay calm for very long. I’ll start talking to myself about what I’m doing, or put music on, or check something on my phone, or suddenly the sketch becomes this whole bigger project with references and colors and… then it’s not really relaxing anymore.

With friends it’s similar, I guess. I can sit there, but I’m not just sitting there, if that makes sense.

Can you describe any situations where you felt like you couldn't control the urge to jump into action before thinking it through, or where you ended up doing something that surprised even you because it felt impulsive?

Yeah… the thing that comes to mind is group brainstorming, especially for design stuff.

Like if someone is explaining an idea, I’ll get excited and kind of jump in before they’re done. Sometimes I’ll blurt out what I think they should add, or if we’re in Figma I might literally start moving things around or adding to their board while they’re still talking. And in my head it feels helpful, like I’m just building on the idea, but then afterward I’m like… oh, that probably came off really pushy.

It’s not like I’m trying to take over. It just feels like the idea is right there and I have to do something with it before it disappears. Then I’ll realize I didn’t really wait for them to finish.

And in my head it feels helpful, like I’m just building on the idea, but then afterward I’m like… oh, that probably came off really pushy.

It’s not like I’m trying to take over. It just feels like the idea is right there and I have to do something with it before it disappears. Then I’ll realize I didn’t really wait for them to finish.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a persistent pattern of inattention and hyperactivity-impulsivity that began in childhood and persists into adulthood, with symptoms present across multiple settings (work, school, home), leading to clinically significant impairment in functioning. There is insufficient evidence for the presence of a primary mood disturbance characteristic of adult-onset disorders like F48.1 (Dysthymia).
